Issued at 434 AM EST Sat Nov 14 2026

PATTERN SYNOPSIS/FORECAST:

Omega block trying to take shape over North America attm...with 
continual waves of troughing digging into the West Coast (120+kt 
upper jet driving some energy across the Desert SW, even)....keeping 
ridge persistent over the central US/Canada...and elongated upper 
low over the eastern US/Canada (530dam upper low over eastern 
Quebec). Shortwave trough swung through last evening with a boost of 
snow showers to show for it; still some niblets of energy to our 
north in the flow over Ontario, though overall, ridging is building 
into our area attm. Moisture wrapping around the back of the upper 
low into our area...with some warm advection through the column, 
particularly in the mid and upper levels; better low-level warm 
advection is to our north over central Canada and Hudson Bay where 
return flow wraps around the surface ridge centered over Ontario. 
Temps remain sufficient for overlake instability and lake effect 
snow showers continue, particularly over NW Lower...with some fine, 
pixie-dust-type snow falling at our office attm as a little bit of 
low/mid-level moisture pivots through. (Some bigger aggregate 
snowflakes around 10-11pm last evening did do their best to 
accumulate, particularly on elevated surfaces.) It is just a touch 
warmer and more moist tonight than it was last night. 

High pressure will continue to slowly build in through the rest of 
the weekend, with lake effect rain/snow showers slowly tapering off 
as the last PV niblets finally depart our area Sunday. Milder 
weather is also anticipated going into early next week as return 
flow strengthens across the central US into the Upper 
Midwest...ahead of more energy digging into the western US. A bit of 
energy tracking across central Canada overtop the ridge early in the 
week looks to scrape off the top of the ridge Monday night into 
Tuesday...with west to southwest winds picking up again. Ridge axis 
builds into the Midwest Tuesday into Wednesday, and return flow 
should have its eyes on us a bit better going into midweek next week 
as a niblet of energy tracks of the longwave trough into the 
Northern Plains/Upper Midwest for the latter half of the week, with 
potential to drive a reasonably developed surface response...and 
will need to keep an eye on this. Signals also point toward 
troughing exiting the western US toward the end of next week, and 
will also need to keep an eye on this...though exactly how this 
evolves is still quite unclear. Bottom line...warmer weather looks 
possible for early/mid week, with increasing chances for active 
weather into the latter half of the week and next weekend.

FORECAST DETAILS...

Lingering Rain/Snow Showers Today, perhaps into Sunday...Moisture 
looks to strip out with time tonight into Sunday...and moisture 
becomes increasingly shallow. Expect this will mainly be a stratocu 
deck, but could squeeze out a bit of precipitation particularly in 
NNW/NW flow belts today as flow becomes more NW aloft...and shifting 
to more westerly going into Sunday. Not much in the way of 
accumulations expected today through the remainder of the weekend, 
maybe a few hundredths of QPF at best...and probably not much more 
in the way of snowfall. This will especially be true tonight into 
Sunday; as we warm aloft through the next 24-36hrs, think we have a 
decent shot at losing ice nucleation, and would not be surprised if 
some areas across the interior ended up seeing a bit of freezing 
drizzle (if they get any precipitation, that is). 

Milder Weather Ahead...Anomalous ridging building into the eastern 
half of North America for the first half of the week should bring 
milder weather back into the region. PV max crossing the area in the 
Monday night-Tuesday timeframe should bring more clouds into the 
region, and if we end up cloudier, we may not get as warm as we 
otherwise could. This being said, it's not impossible the southern 
half of Lower Michigan (perhaps including parts of our CWA) may 
remain relatively unbothered by this feature until more notable warm 
advection enters the scene midweek ahead of the surface system. 
Thermal profiles support potential for highs to reach back into the 
50s...a chance for us procrastinators to get back out and finish up 
those last few yard chores (speaking to myself here too)... though 
with potential for dry air in the region, combined with warmer temps 
and breezy/gusty winds...conditions may not be overly favorable for 
outdoor burning.

Active weather mid to late week...Attm, signals seem to be pointing

going into the middle of the week as a first wave of energy ejects 
out of the western trough. Some uncertainty in how just how 
deep/intense this system will end up...depending particularly on the
